criterion_notes.c1: Examines household and community domestic water supply and sanitation/sewerage service access across all 153 localities (20,221 dwellings; 78,313 inhabitants) in the municipality of Huajuapan de León, Oaxaca.
criterion_notes.c2: Passes the plain wording of Criterion 2 (plain=yes -> plain_criterion2_decision='include'), because the paper characterizes four local water management arrangements ('gestión local del agua': municipal operator SAPAHUA, community-managed Sistemas Independientes de Agua [SIA], tanker trucks, and private wells) and discusses the constitutional/statutory framework (CPEUM Art. 115; Ley de Aguas Nacionales Arts. 44-46; CONAGUA concessions held by 26 of 38 SIAs). However, it FAILS the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading (narrow=no -> decision='exclude', E03): the study's explanatory variable is geodemographic structure (urban/peripheral/rural territorial scale, population density, distance from existing infrastructure, terrain slope/elevation, and geohydrology), which configures which supply modality exists. Statutory provisions are cited only as macro-governance background to critique municipal census aggregation, and neither CONAGUA concession rules, eligibility/tenure rules, nor utility ownership or tariff rules are empirically analyzed as rule-type mechanisms directly governing service access.
criterion_notes.c3: Mixed-methods empirical study combining official census/administrative spatial data (INEGI, SAPAHUA, DECA/RAN), a structured survey of 153 locality representatives (one per locality), and 68 semi-structured interviews with municipal/SAPAHUA officials and community key informants.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports concrete service access outcomes across localities and dwellings, including water supply coverage by provider/modality, piped water in the dwelling, public sewerage connection vs. septic tanks/latrines, payment mode (fixed vs. consumption), and average monthly household water expenditure ($91 to $320 MXN).
criterion_notes.c5: Population and units of analysis (153 localities comprising 78,313 inhabitants and 20,221 dwellings in Huajuapan de León, Oaxaca), exposure (geodemographic characteristics: urban/peripheral/rural location, population density, distance, topography), outcomes (supply/management modality, water and sewerage coverage, monthly expenditure), and cross-sectional mixed-methods geodemographic study design are clearly identifiable.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Spanish (with Spanish and English abstracts); per Criterion 10, translation from the provided 16-page Spanish full text is directly feasible (and would be logged in extraction_note if included).

evidence_quotes.quote: Los resultados evidenciaron la existencia de cuatro formas de acceso y gestión local del agua. De las 153 localidades, 88 tienen abastecimiento de agua por parte del organismo operador municipal que es la SAPAHUA; 38 por Sistemas Independientes de Agua (SIA) gestionados por los mismos habitantes; 17 por pipas trasportadoras de agua, y 10 por pozos de uso particular.

Se evidenció que la gestión del agua varía acorde a las escalas geodemográficas que estructuran el espacio urbano y rural del municipio. En este caso, la población y el territorio configuran los tipos servicio y de gestión que concurren al interior de las comunidades que estructuran el territorio municipal.

With regard to the communities with self-supply from delivery trucks, the central issue is geodemographic. In this case, the necessary population does not exist and the geohydrological conditions of the land are unsuitable for constructing dikes or artesian wells, so the population gets water from delivery trucks.
De los 38 SIA, 26 cuentan con una concesión otorgada por la CONAGUA (LAN, 2016); por tanto, 12 no tienen reconocimiento de la ley, pero sí de los mismos habitantes y el propio gobierno municipal

A total of 153 surveys were conducted for neighborhood presidents, municipal agents or police officers in these communities. Meanwhile, 68 interviews were conducted with key informants in localities with lack of water supply from municipal services, as well as with City Council officers.

Desde el enfoque del hogar, el municipio de Huajuapan de León tiene 20 221 viviendas, con un promedio de 3.84 habitantes por casa. Respecto al suministro, INEGI (2020) reporta que un 93.57% (18,922) de las viviendas tiene abastecimiento de agua entubada dentro de su hogar

raw_response.exposure: Geodemographic and territorial characteristics of localities (urban, peripheral, and rural classification, population density, physical distance from urban infrastructure, topography/elevation, and geohydrological conditions).
raw_response.outcome: Type of local water supply/management modality (municipal SAPAHUA network, community-managed SIA, water delivery trucks, private wells), household/locality water supply and public sewerage coverage, payment mode (fixed vs. consumption), and average monthly water expenditure.
raw_response.population_and_sample: All 153 localities (63 urban, 46 peripheral, 44 rural; total population 78,313 inhabitants in 20,221 dwellings) in the municipality of Huajuapan de León, Oaxaca, Mexico, surveyed via 153 locality key-informant surveys and 68 semi-structured interviews.
raw_response.rationale: Excluded under E03 (Wrong exposure) per the 2026-10-13 narrow rule-type reading of Criterion 2. Although this empirical mixed-methods study examines domestic water and sewerage coverage and monthly household expenditure across 153 localities in Huajuapan de León, Oaxaca, its explanatory focus is geodemographic (how population density, urban/peripheral/rural distance, dispersed settlement, topography, and geohydrology determine whether localities are served by the municipal utility SAPAHUA, community-managed Sistemas Independientes de Agua [SIA], tanker trucks, or private wells). Constitutional and statutory water provisions (CPEUM Art. 115; Ley de Aguas Nacionales Arts. 44-46; CONAGUA concessions) are discussed as macro-governance background showing why municipal census aggregates obscure rural self-supply, rather than empirically analyzing a rule-type legal, administrative, or regulatory mechanism directly governing service access. Under the plain broad wording of Criterion 2, the study would be included (plain_criterion2_decision = 'include') because it characterizes institutional/community water management modalities alongside legal background.
raw_response.study_design: Cross-sectional mixed-methods geodemographic case study combining spatial/census data (INEGI, SAPAHUA, DECA), 153 key-informant locality surveys, and 68 semi-structured interviews.
